text:
Aisha: Quick heads-up: planning a coordinated base-image rebuild next week to apply seccomp profiles, drop setuid, and ship the new compact runtime. We need to lock down signing flow and logging before we flip the registry. Who can take ownership of the signer SA changes?

Ben: I can drive the signer changes. Two options: give the build-runner SA direct KMS sign permission, or introduce an ephemeral signer service that holds only sign rights. I prefer ephemeral service.

Riley: Ephemeral signer sounds safer. Implementation idea: builder posts unsigned artifact to GCS, signer pulls, verifies provenance, then calls KMS sign and writes back attestation. Use STS to mint short-lived creds for signer instances.

Kiran: Agree. Also we need to ensure audit correlation: sign events must include build_id, repo, and pipeline_id so our SIEM can tie KMS logs to the image. KMS audit logs don't include repo metadata by default.

Aisha: Good point. The signer should emit an audit message to the audit-log topic with structured fields (repo, build_id, image_sha, signer_instance). That plus KMS logs gives us deterministic tracing.

Ben: Policy prototype I tested:
```
- role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoSigner
  members:
  - serviceAccount:ephemeral-signer@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- role: roles/logging.logWriter
  members:
  - serviceAccount:ephemeral-signer@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
This restricts sign rights to one SA; the builder only gets `storage.objects.create` for unsigned blobs.

Riley: For least privilege, make signer only able to sign a single key/version. Also rotate key periodically and require Key Access Review entries before granting.

sec-bot: Note: Any new key bindings require KAR approval and an entry in the key inventory. See https://internal.redwood/keys.

Kiran: Re-signing backlog: we'll have thousands of images to re-sign after the rebuild. That could hit KMS per-minute quotas. Proposed mitigation: batch workers with token bucket rate limiter, exponential backoff on 429s, and a maintenance window with a temporary quota bump.

Ben: I'll open the support ticket for quota bump and coordinate with SRE for a maintenance calendar. Also add a dry-run mode in the re-sign workers to estimate quotas.

Aisha: Testing plan: deploy ephemeral-signer to staging, run through 50 sample pipelines, verify cosign/fulcio attestation flow, and confirm the audit-log entries appear in SIEM. If staging looks good, run a small prod canary (10 images) and inspect KMS logs.

Riley: Smoke checks to include:
- cosign verify on canary images
- presence of `sign_event` in audit topic with build_id and repo
- KMS dataAccess entry `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.asymmetricSign` for the key
- registry metadata updated with attestation link

Ben: Example command to check KMS signs:
`gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.AsymmetricSign" AND resource.labels.key_id="projects/.../cryptoKeys/..."' --limit=50`

Kiran: Incident plan: if we see anomalous sign volume (spike or unknown principal), the emergency step is to disable the key via IAM deny policy and pivot to a fallback signing key. We should pre-create a fallback key and add it to the runbook.

Aisha: Add that to runbook. Also include rollback for image verification: we keep old signatures for 48 hours so services can continue to verify while we're rolling.

sec-bot: Action item: Create KAR row for ephemeral-signer SA (assigned to Ben), create quota ticket (assigned to Ben), add fallback key to key inventory (assigned to Kiran), staging smoke tests (Riley).

Riley: I'll add the test harness and a Prometheus exporter that surfaces sign latency, sign errors, and queue depth so we can monitor re-sign progress.

Ben: PR opened: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/ephemeral-signer/+/678 (contains deployment manifest, IAM snippets, and audit-log producer code).

Kiran: One security caveat: make sure signer verifies builder identity (e.g., signed pipeline JWT) before signing; otherwise a compromised builder could get artifacts signed. Also instrument TTL on the unsigned blob so old blobs can't be signed later.

Aisha: Good catch. Add verification and blob expiry. Also require `x-build-id` header and store `x-request-id` in the attestation payload.

Ben: During the maintenance window we'll run a limited re-sign rate and monitor SIEM for any verification failures. If errors exceed threshold, pause the job and open incident channel.

Aisha: Okay team, next steps: Ben files KAR + quota ticket, Riley wires smoke tests and metrics, Kiran creates fallback key and updates runbook. We'll reconvene 24hrs before the window for final go/no-go.

build-bot: Staging deploy scheduled: ephemeral-signer v1.2 -> staging at 2025-11-18T06:00Z.

Aisha: Thanks all. Closing thread after tickets are linked. :white_check_mark:

sec-bot: Tickets created: KAR-452, CLOUD-1290 (quota), RUNBOOK-88 (fallback key).
